a. Reporting periods shall end on the last day of each month.
    b. The permittee is required to submit regular monthly reports no later than the 15th day of

candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of when monthly reporting periods close and when reports are due could change which Federal FY2025 monitoring periods are treated as having required versus missing evidence, affecting monitoring-obligation evaluation (B) and missing-evidence classification for periods without ordinary numeric results (C).

candidates.exact_span:
c. The annual sludge report required in Part IV of the permit is due on February 19 of each
        year and covers the previous calendar year from January 1 through December 31.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this Part IV sludge-reporting obligation is in scope for the selected facilities and how its January–December coverage year maps to Federal FY2025 could change which monitoring requirements are evaluated as applicable versus not required (B).

candidates.exact_span:
If any 30 day average, monthly average, 7 day average, weekly average, or daily maximum
   value exceeds the effluent limitations specified in Part I.A, the permittee shall report the
   excursion in accordance with the requirements of Part III.D.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of which averaging basis (30-day, monthly, 7-day, weekly, daily maximum) applies to a given parameter, and whether a reported value is compared against Part I.A effluent limitations, could change both which numeric limit is used for compliance comparison (A) and whether excursion reporting was required for that measurement (B).

candidates.exact_span:
Any 30 day average, monthly average, 7 day average, weekly average, or daily maximum
   value reported in the required Discharge Monitoring Report which is in excess of the effluent
   limitation specified in Part I.A shall constitute evidence of violation of such effluent
   limitation and of this permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a reported value is treated as an enforceable numeric comparison on the stated averaging period, and whether excess over Part I.A automatically constitutes violation evidence rather than an unresolved or non-comparable result, could change exceedance determinations (A) and how missing or borderline results are classified versus documented violations (C).

candidates.exact_span:
Other measurements of oxygen demand (e.g., TOC and COD) may be substituted for five
   day Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD5) or for five day Carbonaceous Biochemical
   Oxygen Demand (CBOD5), as applicable, where the permittee can demonstrate long term
   correlation of the method with BOD5 or CBOD5 values, as applicable. Details of the
   correlation procedures used must be submitted and prior approval granted by the permitting
   authority for this procedure to be acceptable. Data reported must also include evidence to
   show that the proper correlation continues to exist after approval.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether substitute oxygen-demand parameters (TOC/COD) may be used instead of BOD5/CBOD5—and whether long-term correlation and prior permitting-authority approval are satisfied—could change which enforceable numeric limit applies (A), whether monitoring for the substitute parameter was required or permitted (B), and whether reported substitute values count as adequate evidence or leave applicability unresolved (C).

candidates.exact_span:
The permittee shall report all overflows with the Discharge Monitoring Report submittal. These
reports shall be summarized and reported in tabular format. The summaries shall include: the
date, time, duration, location, estimated volume, and cause of the overflow; observed
environmental impacts from the overflow; actions taken to address the overflow; and ultimate
discharge location if not contained (e.g., storm sewer system, ditch, tributary).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether an overflow event triggers a DMR reporting obligation and what documented overflow details establish about discharge occurrence could change which event-conditioned monitoring requirements are treated as applicable (B) and whether a period is documented as having a discharge versus a no-discharge or insufficient-evidence state (C).

candidates.exact_span:
The permittee shall report any noncompliance which may endanger health or the
environment. Notification shall be made to the EPA at the following e-mail address:
R6_NPDES_Reporting@epa.gov, as soon as possible, but within 24 hours from the time
the permittee becomes aware of the circumstance. Oral notification shall also be to the New
Mexico Environment Department at (505) 827-0187 as soon as possible, but within 24 hours
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of what noncompliance 'may endanger health or the environment' covers, and when the permittee is deemed aware, could change whether 24-hour reporting was required for a given event (B) and whether documented notifications establish a noncompliance or discharge state versus leaving the case unresolved (C).
